newsitem.title: USA: Chevron to settle Texas royalty lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Chevron to settle Texas royalty lawsuit.

text.p: Chevron Corp has agreed to settle a Texas class-action lawsuit alleging underpayment of royalties on oil lifted from state and private land, Texas regulators and a company spokeswoman said on Thursday.

Terms of the settlement will include an unspecified cash payment to the plaintiffs and agreement on a revised system for determining royalties based on published trading prices, the Texas General Land Office said.
"We can confirm that an agreement in principal has been reached," Chevron spokeswoman Jan Golon said.

Filed on behalf of the state's Permanent School Fund, which underwrites state schools with royalties from oil and gas production, the suit was joined by private landowners and charitable trusts which also leased land for oil exploration.
The plaintiffs alleged nine oil companies routinely underpaid royalties by basing payments on posted prices for their oil instead of typically higher market prices.
"Chevron does not concede in the settlement that its current royalty valuation method does not represent the market value of the oil at the lease," Golon said.
Between 1984 and 1994, Chevron paid $42.03 million in royalties to the state school fund, regulators said.

No settlement talks were underway with the remaining defendants -- units of Amoco Corp, Exxon Corp, USX-Marathon Group, Mobil Corp, Phillips Petroleum Co, Shell Oil Co, Texaco Inc and Union Pacific Resources Group Inc -- General Land Office spokesman said.

The Texas land office manages mineral rights on 20.3 million acres of state land and has deposited $6.7 billion in the school fund since its creation in 1854, largely from oil and gas lease bonuses, rentals and royalties.
